rules.title: NJ residential rental application fee cap ($50)
rules.requirement: Landlords or their agents cannot charge an application or similar fee above $50 to apply to lease or sublease a residential rental. The cap is adjusted annually for CPI. Violations carry penalties of up to $500, $750, then $1,000, and the wrongly charged amount is refunded to the applicant.
rules.quoted_span: A landlord, or agent thereof, shall not require an application or other similar fee to apply to lease or sublease a residential rental property for dwelling purposes, which exceeds $50.
rules.effective_date_note: Computed: first day of the fourth month following approval on January 20, 2026.
rules.penalty: Up to $500 first offense, $750 second, $1,000 each subsequent; wrongly charged amount remitted to applicant
rules.exemptions: One-family or two-family dwellings; NJ Real Estate Commission licensees unless they are the landlord.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental property for dwelling purposes.

unverifiable_exemptions: licensee of the NJ Real Estate Commission who is not the landlord

parsed.doc_summary: NJ P.L.2025, c.405 caps residential rental application fees at $50 (CPI-adjusted yearly), with penalties and a refund of wrongly charged amounts. It exempts one- and two-family dwellings and non-landlord real estate licensees. It takes effect 2026-05-01.
